clue.text: One enters playing trill etc, kind of rock singer

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it, so the single letter sits within the reworked letters
letters playing about are rearranged, so trill etc is shuffled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
hard rock is a style of rock music

explanation.surface: A musician trills away while a rock singer of some kind joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges TRILL ETC and 'enters' puts I inside to give LITTLERIC; 'kind of rock' looks like part of the definition but gives HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Richard was the American rock and roll pioneer behind Tutti Frutti.

clue.text: Notice earth and mire around rider?

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
a fox's earth is its den

indicators.note: turned around, so the word for mire is read backwards

parts.note: mire is mud

explanation.surface: A notice warns that earth and mud surround a horse rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rider' is not a horseman: in law a rider is a clause added to a document, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a supplementary clause tacked onto a bill or document, which is an addendum.

clue.text: Scallywag upholding British accent

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means sitting on top of the other piece

parts.note: a scallywag is a rogue

explanation.surface: A rascal props up a British way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a strong regional accent, especially an Irish one.

clue.text: See 1
Drinkers are in this state in empty town

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, here the verb inside the emptied town
an emptied word keeps only its outer letters, its middle removed

parts.note: to state is to aver

explanation.surface: Drinkers are in a certain condition in a deserted town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' reads as a condition such as drunkenness, but it is the verb meaning to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or pub, the place where drinkers gather.

clue.text: Trainee put in ground nuts, at first

parts.note: to inter is to bury, putting a body in the ground

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of nuts is used

explanation.surface: A trainee gardener is told to plant nuts first.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a junior learning on the job, such as a student doctor or work-experience placement.

clue.text: Fool in underwear during time inside home

indicators.note: the underwear comes in the course of, here following, the prison term

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, time spent inside
a bra is an undergarment
at home means in

explanation.surface: A fool sits at home in his underwear while serving time.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD is British slang (from rhyming slang 'bird lime' = time) for a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdbrain is an informal word for a stupid or scatterbrained person.

clue.text: Opener from Sabbath isn't safe, Christian rock

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, taken from Sabbath

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A song opening a Black Sabbath record is too risky to count as Christian rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Christ called Peter the rock on which he would build his church; 'peter' for a safe is safecrackers' slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter's name means stone, and Jesus named this apostle the foundation of the Church.

clue.text: I'll leave the strings vibrating, more than one forte

indicators.note: for a letter to leave is for it to be removed from the rest
vibrating strings are shaken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the I of I'll is the letter that goes

explanation.surface: A musician says they will let the strings resonate, playing loudly throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forte' suggests loud music, but here it means a strong point.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's fortes are the things they are best at, their strong points.

clue.text: See 8
A pair of Frenchmen love contents of magazine

parts.note: MM is the abbreviation for Messieurs, more than one French monsieur
love is zero, the letter O, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Two Frenchmen love what is in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magazine' suggests a periodical, but it is the cartridge holder of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is short for ammunition, the cartridges loaded into a gun's magazine.

clue.text: One member of English rock group, one going on record

definitions.text: One member of English rock group
definitions.meaning: the ... are a row of chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight, so one of them is a ...
a ..., or stylus, sits on a vinyl record as it plays

explanation.surface: A member of an English rock band also makes records.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'rock group' is not a band but THE NEEDLES, chalk rocks off the Isle of Wight on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone stylus is called a needle, and the Needles are pointed chalk rocks.

clue.text: Jersey, perhaps, odd — it's worn by relative

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned word for odd

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone goes round them, so the relative sits inside

parts.note: the it of it's, with 's as a linking is
a nan is a grandmother, a relative

explanation.surface: A jersey jumper looks odd worn by a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' poses as a jumper, but it is the breed of dairy cow, a cud-chewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey cattle chew the cud, making them an example of a ruminant.

clue.text: Clay changed to this mineral in boxes

indicators.note: the phrase mineral in boxes, or contains, the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Clay is turned into a mineral packed in boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassius Clay took the name Muhammad Ali; 'boxes' is also a nod to his sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxer Cassius Clay changed his name to Muhammad Ali in 1964.

clue.text: Name of the game

definitions.meaning: a name or label, such as a graffiti signature
the children's chasing game also called tig or it

explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a label identifying something, and tag is also a playground chasing game.

clue.text: See 18
One who cures fish from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, read from the south means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A man who cures fish caught in southern waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cures' suggests smoking or salting the fish, but means healing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doc is informal for doctor, a person who heals the sick.

clue.text: Twelve months in port

parts.note: twelve months make a year, so twelve gives the A of a year
YR is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone spends a year in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelve months is 'a year', written A YR. Ayr is a harbour town on Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a seaport town on the Firth of Clyde in south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Line dancing by rock singer

indicators.note: dancing letters jig about, so line is rearranged

parts.note: rock is slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: A rock singer joins in the line dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Diamond is the American singer-songwriter of Sweet Caroline and Cracklin' Rosie.

clue.text: Flash car carrying hip, grand rock group

indicators.note: a car carrying something has it inside, so the rest goes within

parts.note: a Rolls, a Rolls-Royce, is a showy car
hip means fashionable, in
G is short for grand, a thousand
a rock is a stone

explanation.surface: A flashy car carries a cool, grand rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock group' looks like the definition, but rock gives STONE and only 'group' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rolling Stones are the long-lived English band led by Mick Jagger.

clue.text: Ladies on staff hiding hotel's way to dodge tax?

parts.note: the ladies is a women's toilet, a loo

indicators.note: the staff hides the letter by holding it inside

parts.note: a staff is a pole
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Female staff at a hotel conceal a scheme for avoiding tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets LOO above the rest in this down clue; 'staff' looks like employees but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is a gap in the rules, commonly exploited to avoid paying tax.

clue.text: Vocabulary of large person once idolised

parts.note: an ex-icon is a former idol

explanation.surface: The language used by a big star of yesteryear.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is the stock of words of a language or person.

clue.text: See 27
A woven fabric to suit oneself

parts.note: twill is a cloth woven with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: A tailor offers a woven cloth for a suit of your choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' hints at tailoring, but 'to suit oneself' means as one pleases.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting at will means doing as you like, whenever you please.

clue.text: Rare bird stopping and starting tours round east

indicators.note: to tour round something is to go all about it, enclosing it

parts.note: on-off describes something that keeps stopping and starting

explanation.surface: A rare bird flits fitfully, circling round to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' suggests birdwatching, but 'rare bird' is an idiom for a unique person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare bird is an exceptional or unique specimen, a one-off with no equal.

clue.text: See 19
Writer's special name for rock once

parts.note: Ayers Rock was the former name of Uluru in central Australia

explanation.surface: A writer's special name for a rock in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L. Sayers was the English novelist who created the detective Lord Peter Wimsey.

clue.text: King, say, in shelter raised part of crown

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards, backwards
the chess piece goes inside the shelter

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind
a king is an example of a chessman, a man

explanation.surface: A king puts up part of his crown in a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The crown is a tooth's, not a monarch's; King is a piece in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is the hard outer layer covering the crown of a tooth.

clue.text: Number of England fans, tolerance-wise, needing reform

indicators.note: letters needing reform are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: England supporters, when it comes to tolerance, need to change their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' means a song: Neil Diamond's Sweet Caroline is sung by England football crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: England football supporters adopted the Neil Diamond song as their stadium anthem.

clue.text: He's in a spy novel, like work of 19 25?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A man appears in a spy novel, reminiscent of the work of a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: Sisyphus endlessly rolled a stone uphill, so his labour is the work of a rolling stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisyphean labour is endless and futile, like Sisyphus forever pushing his boulder up a hill.

clue.text: Some rock singer, when paired with 4

definitions.meaning: ... paired with Richard gives the British singer ... Richard

explanation.definitionFit: A cliff is a sheer rock face, and Cliff Richard is a veteran British pop singer.

clue.text: More refined Conservative right to block maverick

indicators.note: the letter blocks the maverick by sitting inside it

parts.note: a maverick is an outlier, standing apart from the herd

explanation.surface: A refined Tory blocks a rebel on the right of the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtly manners are polished and elegant, so courtlier means more polished.
